correctness.rationale: The recursive complete atomic/extension types characterize the q-round game, proved by induction. Automorphisms permuting indices absent from the chosen tuple make the listed singleton and pair move representatives exhaustive. Two distinct exact implementations agree for every n=1..10 and q=1..5, and a third unreduced checker confirms all n=1..4 at q=5. Complete root types prove each finite cutoff and bridge. A separate support-bijection game proves that all n,m >=2q are rank-q equivalent for every q, joining the finite bridges into the global classification. Code outputs alone are not used to infer an infinite theorem; independent audit is absent.

value.rationale: This is a sharp, complete classification for a standard infinitely growing graph family, not an arbitrary finite slice. The nonuniform five-term cutoff vector (1,3,4,5,7) and the exact seven-class rank-five representative bound of 28 graph vertices identify intrinsic first-order visibility limits. The finite-to-infinite bridge is substantive and reproducible, with a clear motivation from logical distinguishability of standard incidence graphs.
